newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds zone in on Russian blitz after dull day.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds zone in on Russian blitz after dull day.

text.p: Primary market activity was capped by Armistice Day holidays on Monday.
Meanwhile the long-awaited start of Russia's roadshow kicked off in Tokyo and Luxembourg, with hopes of triggering a potential avalanche of demand for Russian assets.
Three teams of finance ministry and central bank officials will criss-cross the globe in what is thought to be the largest effort to woo investors of its kind.
"Turnout is expected to be huge, with hundreds of investors expected in London (on Friday) alone, because interest in Russia is so strong," a banker familiar with the arrangements said.
After waiting in the wings for some time, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett lead-managed a 1.2 billion Swedish crown (around $185 million) asset-backed bond which is backed by housing loans.
The bond, for Saint Goran Securities, has an expected seven-year maturity with a legal maturity of 14-years.

ABN AMRO Hoare Govett syndicate manager said the bond had sold very well to Swedish pension funds with good interest from Norway and Denmark. "We're fully sold out, it is a pity the issue size isn't larger as we've got a lot of unsatisfied demand," he said, adding the asset-backed structure allowed for diversification of financing.

"It is the refinancing of a loan made by the ABN Amro branch in Stockholm to one of the city of Stockholm's housing companies which we have refinanced through the fixed-rate krone market," the ABN AMRO syndicate manager said.
The issue is rated AAA by Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's Corp.

The bond was launched at 50 basis points over the interpolated Swedish government bonds (a blended yield as there is no benchmark in the seven-year Swedish crown sector) and tightened to trade at around 48 b.p. over, dealers said.
